A request comes in → your AI reads the map, opens the right department, pulls what it needs, and does the work — the way an employee would. That's how it handles most of your requests without you in the loop.

One skill does one task. A skill system puts a lead skill in charge of a few skills, so the AI runs a whole job end to end and you only make the final call.

It is one step from your AI Employee, which is the same system once it runs on its own. The skill that builds it is build-skill-system. It maps the job, names every hand-off between steps, and builds the lead skill that runs the rest in order, so you don’t wire anything by hand.

Welcome to the Business X-Ray

The skill that turns your business from a jumble in your head into a clear, visual system you can see, diagnose, and improve.

The Problem

Right now, your business probably lives in your head. You know roughly how things work — how clients find you, what you sell, who helps — but it's all tangled together.

That means when something breaks, you can't see exactly where. When you want to grow, you don't know what to build next. And when someone asks "how does your business work?" — you fumble through a 10-minute explanation.

The core issue: You can't fix what you can't see. And you can't see what's only in your head.

The Solution

The Business X-Ray pulls everything out of your head and turns it into visual diagrams you can point at, discuss, and improve.

Think of it like getting an X-ray at the doctor. The doctor can't fix a broken bone they can't see. Once the X-ray makes the problem visible, the fix becomes obvious. Same principle for your business.

What You'll Learn

This course teaches you the methodology step by step. By the end, you'll understand every diagram, every concept, and every scoring system — so when you run the X-Ray with Claude, you know exactly what it's doing and why.

What Claude Code actually is
Contents

Most people meet AI in a chat box. It answers, you copy the answer out, and it forgets you by tomorrow. Claude Code is a different thing. It's an AI Employee you build that works inside your business and does the job, not just talks about it. This module is the "what" and the "why" before any of the how.

Watch first: what Claude Code is

A plain-English tour of the whole thing. The rest of this course breaks each part down.

💬 The problem with a chat box

A chatbot in a tab is helpful, but it's stuck behind glass. It can't open your files, it doesn't remember your business between chats, and everything it makes you have to copy out and paste somewhere yourself. You get answers, not work that's actually done.

That gap is the whole reason Claude Code exists. It takes the same intelligence out of the tab and puts it to work where your work already lives.

🤖 You employ it, you don't chat with it

What it is. An AI Employee reads and edits your real files, remembers your business in a plain text file, works through multi-step jobs on its own, and runs your exact process instead of generic advice.

💬 A chatbot
Can't see your files

Does one turn at a time
🤖 Your AI Employee
Reads and edits your actual files
Remembers your business (CLAUDE.md)
Does the job, in your tools
Works through multi-step tasks on its own

Why it matters. Everything in this course is just the parts that make that possible. Five of them do most of the work, and you'll meet each one in its own module.

Building block · What it gives your employee
🧠 Memory (CLAUDE.md) · It knows your business, your voice, your rules
🛠️ Skills · Jobs it runs the same way every time
🤖 Sub-agents · Helpers it sends off to work on their own
📡 Connections (MCP) · It reaches your other tools (Notion, Gmail…)
⚡ Hooks · Automatic reactions that keep it reliable

🏆 Why Claude Code, not just Claude.ai

What it is. Claude shows up in a few places. The chat app (Claude.ai) is great for thinking out loud. Cowork hands a task off and waits. Claude Code is the one that becomes a real workforce, because it's the only one with all the parts: skills, sub-agents, your own connections, memory, and the automatic checks.

The point isn't the scoreboard. It's that the building blocks only stack up into an employee in one of these, and that's where we work.

🪟 Where it lives, and why we use VS Code

What it is. It's one engine that runs in several places, the terminal, the desktop app, the web, JetBrains, Slack, and VS Code. They all share the same memory, settings, and connections. We teach it in VS Code for one reason.

Why VS Code. You see everything it does. Every file it reads, every edit it makes, every command it runs shows up in front of you, and you approve or steer in real time. A chatbot is a black box. Claude Code in VS Code is a glass box you can see into.

A workspace is just a folder with a .claude/ folder inside it. That little folder is where your employee's memory, skills, and settings live.

🔁 How it thinks

What it is. Claude Code isn't autocomplete. It works in a loop, like a good new hire. It reads the situation, does the task, checks its own work, and goes again if it's not right yet, until the job is actually done.

"When do I…" — quick cheat sheet

A fast gut-check for which tool fits. (Claude makes these calls with you — this is just so the words make sense.)

…split a skill?

When it's trying to do two jobs and keeps forgetting one. Two jobs → two skills that hand off.

…add a harness?

When a skill works but drifts, or breaks its own rule. An automatic check beats more instructions.

…use an agent?

When the work should run in the background or in parallel — "go do this and report back."

…make a command?

When you do the same thing the same way, often, and want a one-word shortcut.

…put it on autopilot?

When it should run on a schedule or fire on an event, with no one starting it.

…build the next one?

When the current employee is solid on all of the above. Map the next bottleneck and repeat.

What Claude Code actually is
What Claude Code actually is video
Contents

Most people meet AI in a chat box. It answers, you copy the answer out, and it forgets you by tomorrow. Claude Code is a different thing. It's an AI Employee you build that works inside your business and does the job, not just talks about it. This module is the "what" and the "why" before any of the how.

Watch first: what Claude Code is

A plain-English tour of the whole thing. The rest of this course breaks each part down.

💬 The problem with a chat box

A chatbot in a tab is helpful, but it's stuck behind glass. It can't open your files, it doesn't remember your business between chats, and everything it makes you have to copy out and paste somewhere yourself. You get answers, not work that's actually done.

That gap is the whole reason Claude Code exists. It takes the same intelligence out of the tab and puts it to work where your work already lives.

🤖 You employ it, you don't chat with it

What it is. An AI Employee reads and edits your real files, remembers your business in a plain text file, works through multi-step jobs on its own, and runs your exact process instead of generic advice.

💬 A chatbot
Can't see your files
Forgets you between chats
Hands you text to copy-paste
Does one turn at a time
🤖 Your AI Employee
Reads and edits your actual files
Remembers your business (CLAUDE.md)
Does the job, in your tools
Works through multi-step tasks on its own

Why it matters. Everything in this course is just the parts that make that possible. Five of them do most of the work, and you'll meet each one in its own module.

Building block · What it gives your employee
🧠 Memory (CLAUDE.md) · It knows your business, your voice, your rules
🛠️ Skills · Jobs it runs the same way every time
🤖 Sub-agents · Helpers it sends off to work on their own
📡 Connections (MCP) · It reaches your other tools (Notion, Gmail…)
⚡ Hooks · Automatic reactions that keep it reliable

🏆 Why Claude Code, not just Claude.ai

What it is. Claude shows up in a few places. The chat app (Claude.ai) is great for thinking out loud. Cowork hands a task off and waits. Claude Code is the one that becomes a real workforce, because it's the only one with all the parts: skills, sub-agents, your own connections, memory, and the automatic checks.

The point isn't the scoreboard. It's that the building blocks only stack up into an employee in one of these, and that's where we work.

🪟 Where it lives, and why we use VS Code

What it is. It's one engine that runs in several places, the terminal, the desktop app, the web, JetBrains, Slack, and VS Code. They all share the same memory, settings, and connections. We teach it in VS Code for one reason.

Why VS Code. You see everything it does. Every file it reads, every edit it makes, every command it runs shows up in front of you, and you approve or steer in real time. A chatbot is a black box. Claude Code in VS Code is a glass box you can see into.

A workspace is just a folder with a .claude/ folder inside it. That little folder is where your employee's memory, skills, and settings live.

🔁 How it thinks

What it is. Claude Code isn't autocomplete. It works in a loop, like a good new hire. It reads the situation, does the task, checks its own work, and goes again if it's not right yet, until the job is actually done.

And you're never locked out. You can interrupt, steer, or add context at any point, the same way you'd lean over and redirect a teammate mid-task.

…split a skill?

When it's trying to do two jobs and keeps forgetting one. Two jobs → two skills that hand off.

…add a harness?

When the work should run in the background or in parallel — "go do this and report back."

…make a command?

When you do the same thing the same way, often, and want a one-word shortcut.

…put it on autopilot?

When it should run on a schedule or fire on an event, with no one starting it.

When the current employee is solid on all of the above. Map the next bottleneck and repeat.

But "roughly" doesn't give you a roadmap. "Roughly" doesn't tell you what to automate first. "Roughly" keeps you stuck guessing while your competitors stop guessing.

If you went to the doctor in pain, would you want them to guess what's wrong or take an X-ray first? That's what your business needs. Not more guessing. An X-ray.

What the X-Ray Reveals

The Business X-Ray pulls everything out of your head and turns it into visual diagrams. Here's what becomes visible:

Bottlenecks

Where things slow down. The steps that depend entirely on you. If the Owner lane is packed and the AI lane is empty — you are the bottleneck.

AI Opportunities

Repetitive, rules-based work that doesn't need your judgment. These are the steps AI or automation could handle tomorrow — if you knew which ones they were.

Digital Asset Gaps

Written procedures, templates, and sequences your business is missing. Each one you build works 24/7 without you — compounding leverage over time.

High-Value Work

Your strategic superpowers. The work that actually moves the needle. These are the $1,000/hour activities you should protect and never delegate.

The 30-Day Test

Ask yourself: If you went on holiday for 30 days, which parts of your business would stop? Everything that stops = a single point of failure. Everything that keeps running = a system. The X-Ray shows you the ratio.

What Mapping Forces You to Do
1. Get It Out of Your Head

When it's in your head, it's invisible. When it's on a diagram, it becomes a thing you can point at, discuss, and improve. You stop being the system and start seeing the system.

2. Be Brutally Specific

Instead of "I do marketing," you write: "I post YouTube videos that drive traffic to a free guide download page that feeds into an email sequence." Specifics reveal gaps.

3. See What's Missing

Empty columns mean something is missing. A full "Owner" row means you're the bottleneck. Connections without systems mean things are falling through cracks.

In Cowork only.

Do this now Open the Cowork Project that will hold your Business OS, then run one command.

For a new workspace, use New chat → Project → Add folder and choose a permanent business folder. If you already have a workspace, reopen that Project with the same folder attached. Leave this page open while Claude connects AIEB, checks your saved intake, and verifies the workspace can persist there.

Copy
/ai-employee-builder:setup-aieb
Prefer to watch first? Open the 10-minute walkthrough

1. Attach the folder before setup starts.

New workspace: choose New chat → Project → Add folder, then select a permanent folder you can find again.
Returning workspace: open its existing Cowork Project and confirm the same folder is attached. Do not create a second workspace.
Existing files in the folder: Claude should name the folder and ask before changing it. If the folder is read-only or the workspace lives elsewhere, reconnecting AIEB can still succeed, but workspace setup must wait until the correct writable folder is attached.

2. In that Cowork Project chat, type /ai-employee-builder:setup-aieb and select that plugin skill. Then press Enter again (or click Start task) to run it. After selection, Cowork may shorten the chip to /setup-aieb — that is normal. If slash commands are unavailable, say “Set up AIEB”.

3. If Cowork shows an AIEB Connect action, click it.

Already signed into this course? Continue with that account. The server matches the verified member and active subscription already stored in AIEB.
Otherwise, continue with Google using the address attached to your purchase. A returning member reconnects without consuming a second activation merely because Cowork changed runtimes.
If the purchase cannot be matched, use the Lemon Squeezy key from your receipt on the secure page only. Never paste it into Claude.
If Cowork says the authorization expired but still shows AIEB as Connected, open Customize → Connectors → aieb, disconnect that stale entry, then reconnect. Do not disconnect a healthy connector just to update the plugin.
Return to the same Cowork Project chat when the browser says connected. The paid tool retries with the host-managed connection.

4. Back in the chat, the setup task checks your Get Access intake.

Already completed it? Claude uses the four saved answers and does not ask them again.
Not completed yet? Claude asks, one at a time, what your business sells, which recurring job you want to remove, how often it happens and how much time it takes, and what a good finished result looks like.
After the fourth answer, Claude calls complete_aieb_onboarding and confirms your onboarding is saved before continuing.

5. Wait for the persistence check before calling the workspace ready. Claude should:

Name the Project folder it is using
Create only the AIEB workspace frame your access supports, after confirming a non-empty folder is the right place
Read the saved state back from that same folder and confirm it will be available in your next Project chat

Success has two separate checks: AIEB says the connector and paid access are verified, then names the attached folder and confirms the workspace state was saved and read back there. A connected connector by itself does not mean the workspace is ready. Connecting Notion, Drive, email, and other business tools is the separate next step.

Before the Business X-Ray, watch this overview — it shows how handing AI one map of your business turns it from a tool you babysit into an employee that runs the work. Below the video is exactly why that map matters and how it works — then two quick questions to continue.

Why you give AI a Business Map

A business map is one file plus a set of department folders — a model of how your whole business runs and how it makes money (Leads → Appointments → Presentations → Sales). It's the single thing that turns AI from a tool into an employee.

Without a map

Your AI doesn't know where anything lives or how you make money, so you hand-hold every task. You stay the router — every request runs through you.

With a map (how it works)

A request comes in → your AI reads the map, opens the right department, pulls what it needs, and does the work — the way an employee would. That's how it handles most of your requests without you in the loop.

A skill is a reusable playbook you write once so the AI does a task your way, every time. Same input, same quality, no re-explaining. It is the unit everything else here is built from.

What a skill system is

One skill does one task. A skill system puts a lead skill in charge of a few skills, so the AI runs a whole job end to end and you only make the final call.

It is one step from your AI Employee, which is the same system once it runs on its own. The skill that builds it is build-skill-system. It maps the job, names every hand-off between steps, and builds the lead skill that runs the rest in order, so you don’t wire anything by hand.

Slide 1 of 6

Everything you build lives in one of two homes. A workflow is a file inside one skill, like the weekly and launch versions inside draft-email, and only that skill ever opens it. A shared skill gets its own folder, and any lead skill can call it. Follow the arrows. Weekly-email and launch-email both call the same draft-email and qa-draft, so you build each one once.

Review + harden

Before you let it run alone, tighten it. Hardening makes the skill check its own work and fail loudly instead of quietly, so you can trust the output without re-reading every line.

An unhardened skill does not break. It hands you something slightly wrong and says nothing.

Your rules are already in the file, so hardening is really just a check that holds every draft to them before it reaches you.

Slide 1 of 5

Two ways this week’s email can go wrong. On the left it breaks loudly. The AI tells you it could not open your stats file, you see it straight away, and nothing goes out. Look at the right-hand one instead. It reads perfectly and has one number in it that was never in your stats. That is the one that reaches your list with your name on it.

What Claude Code actually is

Most people meet AI in a chat box. It answers, you copy the answer out, and it forgets you by tomorrow. Claude Code is a different thing. It's an AI Employee you build that works inside your business and does the job, not just talks about it. This module is the "what" and the "why" before any of the how.

Watch first: what Claude Code is

A plain-English tour of the whole thing. The rest of this course breaks each part down.

💬 The problem with a chat box

A chatbot in a tab is helpful, but it's stuck behind glass. It can't open your files, it doesn't remember your business between chats, and everything it makes you have to copy out and paste somewhere yourself. You get answers, not work that's actually done.

That gap is the whole reason Claude Code exists. It takes the same intelligence out of the tab and puts it to work where your work already lives.

🤖 You employ it, you don't chat with it

What it is. An AI Employee reads and edits your real files, remembers your business in a plain text file, works through multi-step jobs on its own, and runs your exact process instead of generic advice.

💬 A chatbot
Can't see your files
Forgets you between chats
Hands you text to copy-paste
Does one turn at a time
🤖 Your AI Employee
Reads and edits your actual files
Remembers your business (CLAUDE.md)
Does the job, in your tools
Works through multi-step tasks on its own

Why it matters. Everything in this course is just the parts that make that possible. Five of them do most of the work, and you'll meet each one in its own module.

Building block · What it gives your employee
🧠 Memory (CLAUDE.md) · It knows your business, your voice, your rules
🛠️ Skills · Jobs it runs the same way every time
🤖 Sub-agents · Helpers it sends off to work on their own
📡 Connections (MCP) · It reaches your other tools (Notion, Gmail…)
⚡ Hooks · Automatic reactions that keep it reliable

🏆 Why Claude Code, not just Claude.ai

What it is. Claude shows up in a few places. The chat app (Claude.ai) is great for thinking out loud. Cowork hands a task off and waits. Claude Code is the one that becomes a real workforce, because it's the only one with all the parts: skills, sub-agents, your own connections, memory, and the automatic checks.

The point isn't the scoreboard. It's that the building blocks only stack up into an employee in one of these, and that's where we work.

🪟 Where it lives, and why we use VS Code

What it is. It's one engine that runs in several places, the terminal, the desktop app, the web, JetBrains, Slack, and VS Code. They all share the same memory, settings, and connections. We teach it in VS Code for one reason.

Why VS Code. You see everything it does. Every file it reads, every edit it makes, every command it runs shows up in front of you, and you approve or steer in real time. A chatbot is a black box. Claude Code in VS Code is a glass box you can see into.

A workspace is just a folder with a .claude/ folder inside it. That little folder is where your employee's memory, skills, and settings live.

🔁 How it thinks

What it is. Claude Code isn't autocomplete. It works in a loop, like a good new hire. It reads the situation, does the task, checks its own work, and goes again if it's not right yet, until the job is actually done.

And you're never locked out. You can interrupt, steer, or add context at any point, the same way you'd lean over and redirect a teammate mid-task.

Welcome to the Business X-Ray

The skill that turns your business from a jumble in your head into a clear, visual system you can see, diagnose, and improve.

The Problem

Right now, your business probably lives in your head. You know roughly how things work — how clients find you, what you sell, who helps — but it's all tangled together.

That means when something breaks, you can't see exactly where. When you want to grow, you don't know what to build next. And when someone asks "how does your business work?" — you fumble through a 10-minute explanation.

The core issue: You can't fix what you can't see. And you can't see what's only in your head.

The Solution

The Business X-Ray pulls everything out of your head and turns it into visual diagrams you can point at, discuss, and improve.

Think of it like getting an X-ray at the doctor. The doctor can't fix a broken bone they can't see. Once the X-ray makes the problem visible, the fix becomes obvious. Same principle for your business.

What You'll Learn

This course teaches you the methodology step by step. By the end, you'll understand every diagram, every concept, and every scoring system — so when you run the X-Ray with Claude, you know exactly what it's doing and why.

What Claude Code actually is
What Claude Code actually is video
Contents

Most people meet AI in a chat box. It answers, you copy the answer out, and it forgets you by tomorrow. Claude Code is a different thing. It's an AI Employee you build that works inside your business and does the job, not just talks about it. This module is the "what" and the "why" before any of the how.

Watch first: what Claude Code is

A plain-English tour of the whole thing. The rest of this course breaks each part down.

💬 The problem with a chat box

A chatbot in a tab is helpful, but it's stuck behind glass. It can't open your files, it doesn't remember your business between chats, and everything it makes you have to copy out and paste somewhere yourself. You get answers, not work that's actually done.

That gap is the whole reason Claude Code exists. It takes the same intelligence out of the tab and puts it to work where your work already lives.

🤖 You employ it, you don't chat with it

What it is. An AI Employee reads and edits your real files, remembers your business in a plain text file, works through multi-step jobs on its own, and runs your exact process instead of generic advice.

💬 A chatbot
Can't see your files
Forgets you between chats
Hands you text to copy-paste
Does one turn at a time
🤖 Your AI Employee
Reads and edits your actual files
Remembers your business (CLAUDE.md)
Does the job, in your tools
Works through multi-step tasks on its own

Why it matters. Everything in this course is just the parts that make that possible. Five of them do most of the work, and you'll meet each one in its own module.

Building block · What it gives your employee
🧠 Memory (CLAUDE.md) · It knows your business, your voice, your rules
🛠️ Skills · Jobs it runs the same way every time
🤖 Sub-agents · Helpers it sends off to work on their own
📡 Connections (MCP) · It reaches your other tools (Notion, Gmail…)
⚡ Hooks · Automatic reactions that keep it reliable

🏆 Why Claude Code, not just Claude.ai

What it is. Claude shows up in a few places. The chat app (Claude.ai) is great for thinking out loud. Cowork hands a task off and waits. Claude Code is the one that becomes a real workforce, because it's the only one with all the parts: skills, sub-agents, your own connections, memory, and the automatic checks.

The point isn't the scoreboard. It's that the building blocks only stack up into an employee in one of these, and that's where we work.

🪟 Where it lives, and why we use VS Code

What it is. It's one engine that runs in several places, the terminal, the desktop app, the web, JetBrains, Slack, and VS Code. They all share the same memory, settings, and connections. We teach it in VS Code for one reason.

Why VS Code. You see everything it does. Every file it reads, every edit it makes, every command it runs shows up in front of you, and you approve or steer in real time. A chatbot is a black box. Claude Code in VS Code is a glass box you can see into.

A workspace is just a folder with a .claude/ folder inside it. That little folder is where your employee's memory, skills, and settings live.

🔁 How it thinks

What it is. Claude Code isn't autocomplete. It works in a loop, like a good new hire. It reads the situation, does the task, checks its own work, and goes again if it's not right yet, until the job is actually done.

And you're never locked out. You can interrupt, steer, or add context at any point, the same way you'd lean over and redirect a teammate mid-task.

"When do I…" — quick cheat sheet

A fast gut-check for which tool fits. (Claude makes these calls with you — this is just so the words make sense.)

…split a skill?

When it's trying to do two jobs and keeps forgetting one. Two jobs → two skills that hand off.

…add a harness?

When a skill works but drifts, or breaks its own rule. An automatic check beats more instructions.

…use an agent?

When the work should run in the background or in parallel — "go do this and report back."

…make a command?

When you do the same thing the same way, often, and want a one-word shortcut.

…put it on autopilot?

When it should run on a schedule or fire on an event, with no one starting it.

…build the next one?

When the current employee is solid on all of the above. Map the next bottleneck and repeat.

Already completed it? Claude uses the four saved answers and does not ask them again.
Not completed yet? Claude asks, one at a time, what your business sells, which recurring job you want to remove, how often it happens and how much time it takes, and what a good finished result looks like.
After the fourth answer, Claude calls complete_aieb_onboarding and confirms your onboarding is saved before continuing.

Name the Project folder it is using
Create only the AIEB workspace frame your access supports, after confirming a non-empty folder is the right place
Read the saved state back from that same folder and confirm it will be available in your next Project chat
